subject: gov.policy
name: CEMAC Regional Financial Inclusion Strategy (SRIF) 2025-2029
milestone: Published by BEAC, February 2025, validated by the UMAC Ministerial Committee on 21 December 2023
position_start: Did not exist; national financial-inclusion strategies existed only in Chad, Cameroon and the Central African Republic, and no member state had a national financial-education strategy
position_end: Sets a financial-inclusion target of 60% by 2029 and 75% by 2032, against a 32% baseline in 2021; six strategic axes and 68 actions across 24 objectives, budgeted at FCFA 43.8bn; developed over 30 months with more than 200 stakeholders across the six member states, World Bank-financed via a regional-institutions capacity project

subject: gov.legislate
name: CEMAC free-movement regime (Additional Act of 2019)
milestone: National implementing instructions issued in the Central African Republic (23 September 2024) and Cameroon (18 September 2024)
position_start: Additional act of 1 April 2019 exempts nationals of the six member states from visas for stays up to 90 days on presentation of a biometric national ID, CEMAC ID, biometric passport or approved CEMAC passport
position_end: Five years after enactment, two national police instructions applied it for the first time, following the fourth CCPAC (Central African police chiefs' committee) security session in Yaoundé; Gabon and Equatorial Guinea are named as continuing to refuse application
note: The refusal is attributed by the source to three named public narratives ("myths") in Gabon and Equatorial Guinea; the underlying academic study behind that attribution is not held

subject: gov.legislate
name: ECCAS free-movement protocol (Annex VII, 1983 Treaty)
milestone: Scholarly implementation analysis published 19 February 2024
position_start: ECCAS founded 18 October 1983 by the former UDEAC members plus the CEPGL states, Angola and Sao Tome and Principe, carrying a free-movement-of-persons-and-goods annex from the outset
position_end: Annex VII is found not effectively implemented over four decades, attributed to poor infrastructure and communication links, political instability and rivalry between heads of state, and routine roadblocks within and across borders; ECCAS itself hibernated 1992-1998
sources: 2024-02-19 Challenges to the Implementation of Regional Integration in ECCAS
note: A distinct instrument from CEMAC's own 2019 free-movement act above; the same six core states sit under both, with different delivery records

subject: gov.protect
name: CEMAC Regulation 01/20 on protection of banking consumers
milestone: Adopted 3 July 2020, in force 1 January 2021, mediation provisions from 1 January 2023
position_end: Community consumer-protection rules for users of banking, microfinance and payment services across the six member states: fair treatment, information and transparency duties, contractual balance, data-protection duties, complaint-handling and mediation

subject: gov.regional
name: Africa CDC Central Africa health-data sharing roadmap
milestone: Regional advocacy workshop closed in Libreville, 21 August 2026
position_end: Roadmap sets a six-week deadline for drafting an inter-country convention on cross-border health-data sharing and a four-week deadline for a formal sharing mechanism, to be put to the health ministers of the seven of nine Central African member states that have yet to sign the underlying protocol, after experts worked through data-protection, confidentiality and sovereignty obstacles

subject: gov.regional
name: ARTAC (Central African Telecommunications Regulators Conference)
milestone: 10th Ordinary Session held in Kinshasa, reported 24 February 2026
position_start: A standing regional regulators' body with no dated recent record held
position_end: 10th Ordinary Session (Kinshasa) adopted revised statutes, internal regulations and financial rules, extended the Executive Committee's mandate to December 2027, recommended a harmonised NGSO framework requiring satellite providers (Starlink, OneWeb, Amazon Kuiper named) to establish terrestrial gateways within ARTAC's jurisdiction and keep citizens' data stored within Africa, and mandated free roaming across Central Africa by 30 June 2026; separately co-organised a sub-regional fibre-infrastructure mapping workshop with the ITU in N'Djamena, 15-18 December 2025
note: ARTAC has no entity page in the base; the NGSO recommendation is provider-agnostic in form but its named targets are all US/UK operators

subject: gov.regional
name: Cameroon-Chad digital cooperation agreement
milestone: Concluded after a four-day technical mission, 16 May 2025
position_end: Concluded between the two communications ministries as a bilateral step inside the region's digital integration (2025-05)

subject: gov.regional
name: Central Africa regional digital market policy and framework law 2025-2030
milestone: Texts produced at the regional workshop, Douala, 24 September 2025
position_end: A regional workshop attended by all ten member states of the economic community plus the monetary community produced a 2025-2030 regional digital-trade policy and a framework law covering harmonised data-protection and cybersecurity rules and free movement of data across the region's economic space; both texts await political endorsement and no endorsement date is published

subject: gov.regional
name: Regional harmonisation of remittance policies (ECCAS)
milestone: Country diagnostics published, April 2025
position_end: Country diagnostics on remittance policy and its regional harmonisation, on data through November 2023 (2025-04)
sources: 2025-04-01 Regional Harmonization of Remittance Policies in ECCAS - Burundi
note: A diagnostic, not an instrument; no harmonised rule has been adopted.

subject: gov.standards
name: CEMAC interoperable QR-code payment standard
milestone: Community standard launched at Douala, 29 July 2026, under Reglement N 02/26/CEMAC/UMAC/CORENOFI of 8 April 2026
position_start: Piloted nationally as Gabon's MaDigiPaie QR code, launched Libreville 9 December 2025 with more than 1,000 codes deployed at launch
position_end: BEAC and GIMAC launched the community-wide interoperable QR code at Douala, letting any bank, microfinance or mobile-money app scan any merchant's code across all six states through GIMACPAY to EMVCo standards, with 24 institutions already in production as at 29 July; GIMACPAY carried 20.3m transactions worth FCFA 863bn in 2025 (+40% by volume) across 153 participants; a tariff-revision workshop opened 30 July, cutting interoperability tariffs and capping merchant payments at 1%, not yet in force (hoped for 1 January 2027); merchant payment remains under 1% of interoperable traffic (48,605 transactions, FCFA 9.7bn, Q1 2026). The ministerial committee that adopted the regulation homologated standards for automated bills of exchange and automatic direct debit alongside the QR code, so the instrument is wider than this row's name
note: The regulation's own text is not held, only its citation, so what it obliges participants to do beyond the launch account is unestablished The adopting communique is now held, though the regulation text is still not.

subject: gov.standards
name: GIMAC PCI DSS v4.0.1 certification
milestone: Certification renewed, issued by assessor DATAPROTECT, March 2026
position_start: Certified under a prior PCI DSS version
position_end: GIMAC's card-data processing and transmission infrastructure recertified to PCI DSS v4.0.1

subject: gov.standards
name: ISO 20022 adoption across the community payment systems
milestone: Governor's Instruction 001/GR/2025 of 17 November 2025
position_end: The central bank mandated community-wide adoption of ISO 20022 messaging - cross-border payments rules for international flows and bank-specific formats for the two regional payment systems - on a migration timetable running from November 2025 to May 2026, and a companion circular put the message specifications online through a closed community area of the messaging network's standards portal
note: No completion of the migration is reported in the base.

subject: gov.discourse
name: Independent research on the region's digital systems
milestone: Rural backhaul cost analysis published, July 2026
position_start: Scattered work with no standing body of regional analysis
position_end: Three independent accounts inside a year: criminal capture of a cryptocurrency scheme in the Central African Republic, a country study finding the Republic of Congo's digital ambitions will stall without policy change, and an analysis attributing triple-cost rural connectivity to backhaul spectrum fees (2026-07)
sources: 2026-07-16-congo-rural-backhaul-spectrum-fees-techafricanews|2026-06-22 Driving Digital Transformation of the Economy in the Republic of Congo|2025-12-01-gitoc-behind-the-blockchain-crypto-criminal-capture-globalinitiative

subject: finance.new
name: Digital Business Boost for Africa grant
milestone: Grant convention signed, 2026
position_end: A EUR 15m European Union grant, stated as FCFA 9.83bn, covering Cameroon, Gabon, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Congo, to strengthen the foundations of a safe, inclusive and sustainable digital economy; the implementing bank is named only by nationality and no country split, component list or delivery date is published

subject: infra.connect
name: Central Africa Peering Forum
milestone: Scheduled for Yaounde, 30 September-1 October 2026
position_end: Central Africa's own regional peering event, covering peering, interconnection, routing security and RPKI, closing a 2026 calendar that already ran West Africa's forum in Cotonou (June) and the continental AfPIF in Kigali (August)

subject: infra.connect
name: Central African Backbone
milestone: Cameroon sought USD 195 million for backbone expansion under a presidential decree of March 2026
position_start: National segments built and interconnected — the Central African Republic's national backbone inaugurated in February 2023 with an interconnection to Congo
position_end: Extending in three directions at once: Congo's 600 km backbone linking Cameroon and the Central African Republic, Cameroon seeking USD 195 million to expand its own, and Congo Telecom stating an ambition to lead regional digital transit (2026-06)
sources: 2026-06-21-congo-telecom-central-africa-digital-hub-ambition-techreviewafrica|2026-03-09-seeks-195-million-optic-fibre-backbone-eximbank-china-itweb|2023-02-08-afdb-inauguration-dorsale-optique-nationale-rca|2024-05-20 Congo to build Central Africa's first fibre data centre (Brazzaville, $72.8m)
note: The Central African Republic is separately seeking a link through South Sudan to reduce its dependence on these routes.

subject: infra.connect
name: Central African Republic interconnection through South Sudan
milestone: Announced by the authorities, May 2026
position_end: Announced to reduce dependence on fragile regional networks and improve access to international capacity (2026-05)
note: No route, financing or timetable is stated. It would take the region's most isolated member out through East Africa rather than through CEMAC.

subject: infra.connect
name: Nigeria-Equatorial Guinea subsea cable
milestone: Agreement signed, February 2026
position_end: Signed to expand broadband capacity and regional cybersecurity between West and Central Africa (2026-02)
sources: 2026-02-24 Nigeria, Equatorial Guinea subsea cable strengthens connectivity
note: No landing date, capacity or ownership structure is stated.

subject: infra.store
name: National data centres across the region
milestone: Gabon inaugurated the region's first Tier III facility, July 2026
position_start: One national data centre under construction at Brazzaville, about 60 per cent complete in May 2024
position_end: Four national builds running: Brazzaville at USD 72.8 million and 90 per cent complete by August 2025 for a November launch, Gabon's first Tier III facility inaugurated in July 2026, Cameroon's carrier facility drawing central-bank interest, and Chad negotiating one with Azerbaijan (2026-07)
sources: 2026-07-06 Gabon Inaugurates First Tier III Datacenter to Boost Digital Sovereignty|2025-08-06-datacenter-national-inaugure-novembre-ldb|2025-08-07-congo-national-data-centre-90pc-november-launch-techafricanews|2025-03-04-congo-national-data-centre-80pc-complete-wearetech|2024-05-17-afdb-congo-national-data-centre-digital-sovereignty|2024-05-20 Congo to build Central Africa's first fibre data centre (Brazzaville, $72.8m)|2025-12-17-beac-national-director-visits-camtel-data-center-techreviewafrica|2026-06-12-camtel-zamengoe-data-centre-sovereignty-sago-techreviewafrica|2025-12-02 Chad Accelerates Digital Cooperation to Support Its Transformation Agenda
note: Every one of the four is framed by its own government as digital sovereignty. No commissioning confirmation for the Brazzaville facility's November 2025 launch is held.

subject: infra.store
name: PIDA data-centre infrastructure prospectus (ECCAS)
milestone: Prospectus published 25 August 2026
position_end: The AU's Programme for Infrastructure Development in Africa (PIDA) published a project prospectus for data-centre infrastructure development framed at ECCAS/regional level, underpinning the digital economy; no financing, sponsor or timetable is stated in the prospectus itself

subject: infra.cybersec
name: ITU regional Cyberdrill (Central Africa)
milestone: 13th edition opened at Kintele (Congo), 1 July 2025, closed 7 July 2025
position_end: 13th ITU regional Cyberdrill convened agencies and defence forces from across Central Africa to test cross-border incident response; Congo's Prime Minister framed national cybersecurity as a sovereignty question at the opening, and Congo's ANSSI is named as the government's technical arm; ITU's own loss and attack-rate figures cited at the opening are not independently held; a first Central Africa cybersecurity conference was separately announced for Brazzaville in June 2026, with no further detail published

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Central Africa Credit Information Bureau (CICA)
milestone: Operational launch at Douala, 20 January 2026
position_start: Authorised as the community credit information bureau by Governor's Decision 142/GR/2025 of 25 November 2025
position_end: Launched by the central bank with an international finance institution on a hub-and-spokes model based in Douala, with 61 financial institutions across the six member states connected to the test platform - a community-wide regime for sharing borrower credit data across borders
note: The authorisation decision text itself is not held, only the bureau's own page reporting it.

subject: dpi.exchange
name: I-CEMAC (INTERPOL border-management project)
milestone: Ongoing project, 2019-2024, EUR4.9m, funded by CEMAC
position_start: Project launched 2019, targeting extension of INTERPOL's I-24/7 network and databases to 40 border points and modernisation of all six CEMAC national INTERPOL bureaux
position_end: Gabon completed four border posts with automated database searches (Eboro, Myo-Kye, Leconi, Port-Gentil, March 2024); Equatorial Guinea extended I-24/7 to ten sites including the Malabo, Bata and Mongomeyen airports; Cameroon's connected sites (Douala/Yaounde) logged more than 6,000 searches in 72 hours
note: Date precision is year-level (proxy), not day-level, on this record

subject: dpi.pay
name: BEAC accession to PAPSS
status: Implemented, not yet operational for members
milestone: Accession reported 9-10 July 2026
position_end: BEAC formally joined PAPSS, extending the continental real-time cross-border settlement rail into the CEMAC zone, with CEMAC banks' integration targeted by end-2026; as at 25 August, Cameroonian businesses report no operational access, and no public list of operational Cameroonian banks, open corridors, tariffs or ceilings has been published

subject: dpi.pay
name: CEMAC payment services report
milestone: 2024 edition published by the central bank, April 2026
position_start: Published annually by the central bank
position_end: Published for 2024 as the zone's statistical account of payment services (2026-04)
sources: 2026-04-08-beac-rapport-services-paiement-cemac-2024|2025-11-01 SIIPS 2025 State of Inclusive Instant Payment Systems in Africa

subject: dpi.pay
name: CEMAC Regulation 04/18 on payment services
milestone: Adopted 21 December 2018, in force 1 January 2019
position_end: The founding community act for payment services across the six member states: it assigns the central bank rulemaking and technical-standards power and the banking commission prudential-supervisory and sanctioning power over payment service providers, and sets the pre-contractual and contractual protections for users of digital payment and electronic money
note: The base holds two captures of this one regulation; the fuller of the two is cited first, the other being truncated at capture.

subject: dpi.pay
name: Central bank instruction on inbound remittance pre-financing
milestone: Instruction 002/GR/2026 of 5 May 2026
position_end: Supplementing the community payment-services regulation, credit institutions must verify on concordant bank and messaging-network evidence that inbound remittance pre-financing executed through payment institutions has been matched by repayment - a rule bearing directly on the safety of funds credited to electronic-money wallets

subject: dpi.pay
name: GIMACPAY interoperability platform
milestone: Commercial launch 10 July 2020 under Governor's Instruction 001/GR/2018
position_end: The community's converged card, mobile and money-transfer interoperability platform, operated across the six member states by the regional interbank grouping and carrying 79 participants on the operator's own description
note: The rail the community QR-code standard and the regional retail-payment platform both run over.

subject: dpi.pay
name: Licensing of new payment providers in the zone
milestone: Aggregator licence granted in Congo, June 2026
position_start: A payments unicorn licensed in Cameroon through a bank partnership (2025-06)
position_end: Four entrants licensed or partnered inside a year: a payments company in Cameroon through a bank partnership, a card network with a Cameroonian bank, a fintech with the International Finance Corporation in Chad, and a payment aggregator formally recognised in Congo (2026-06)

subject: dpi.pay
name: SYSTAC 2 (BEAC regional retail-payment platform)
milestone: Entered production 3 August 2026, per BEAC's own communique of 12 August
position_start: A retail clearing platform in service since 2007
position_end: Centralised, fully online ISO 20022-compliant platform for transfers, direct debits, cheques and card payments across all six CEMAC states, with strengthened AML/KYC and a dedicated dispute-resolution module; the instant-payments module is explicitly not yet in production, no date given; the RTGS successor SYGMA V10 is described only as coming "in the coming weeks", also undated
note: A trade-press account misdated the launch to 2027; BEAC's own communique settles it to 3 August 2026

subject: dpi.pay
name: Taxation of mobile money in the CEMAC zone
milestone: Central bank opposed excessive taxation publicly, March 2026
position_start: Mobile money taxed at national discretion with no stated regional position
position_end: The central bank came out firmly against excessive taxation of mobile money, warning that transaction taxes penalise low-income households and hold back financial inclusion, and called for a concerted approach (2026-03)
note: The bank states a position; no member state's tax has been changed on the record, and the regional financial-inclusion strategy targets 60 per cent by 2029.

subject: dpi.registry
name: Reference Manual for Civil Registration and Vital Statistics Systems in Central Africa
milestone: Adopted by the union council of ministers at Brazzaville, June 2026
position_end: A common framework for registering births and other vital events across the member states, prepared under a World Bank-financed statistical programme with United Nations population-fund support; no implementation date, member-state adoption count or registration target is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Regional support for birth registration
milestone: Support restated at the eighth African civil registration conference, August 2025
position_end: The Francophonie organisation restated continuing support for advancing birth registration across Central Africa (2025-08)
sources: 2025-08-12 La Francophonie supports birth registration efforts across Central Africa, Madagascar
note: A statement of support; no registration rate, target or programme figure for the region is held.

subject: tech.ai
name: AfroLeadership proposal to integrate AU data governance into CEMAC AI policy
milestone: Civil-society policy brief published 11 November 2025
position_end: AfroLeadership argues the AU Data Policy Framework and a data-justice lens should shape how the CEMAC six approach AI governance, on the ground that AI systems process data at a scale existing governance mechanisms were not built for; the brief itself frames CEMAC as the regional economic community least represented in the wiki's AI material
note: A civil-society proposal, not an adopted instrument or a body decision

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Media and information literacy digital-skills project
status: Discontinued, closed at its scheduled end
milestone: Scheduled end date 31 December 2025
position_end: A USD 166,800 regional project on media and information literacy and digital skills, reported at 66% overall progress with USD 109,943 spent as it reached its scheduled end; no output, reach or evaluation figure is published

subject: capacity.training
name: African Institute of Informatics (IAI-Cameroun)
milestone: Visited by the regional commission for human development, 4 August 2026
position_end: Operating as an inter-state training institution, with the regional commission opening collaboration on education and digital skills (2026-08)

subject: include.access
name: Economic inclusion of refugees in Central Africa
milestone: Technical report for the regional value-chains project
position_end: Diagnosed under the regional inclusive and resilient value chains project, following a private-sector-for-refugees framework (2024)

subject: data.statistics
name: BEAC 2026 balance-of-payments data collection
milestone: Collection launched, reported 22 April 2026
position_end: BEAC launched the data-collection phase of its 2026 balance-of-payments exercise across the CEMAC zone; no completion date or published output yet

subject: data.statistics
name: CEMAC harmonised labour-statistics framework
milestone: Nine-day CEMAC/ILO workshop closed in Pointe-Noire, 27 August 2026 (opened 19 August)
position_start: No CEMAC member state runs a regular labour force survey, on the organisers' own statement
position_end: World Bank-financed HISWACA workshop, with ILO technical support, produced a regional methodological guide and a preliminary roadmap for quarterly labour-force surveys across the six member states; CEMAC put informal employment above 65% of jobs bloc-wide and unemployment ranging from 1.1% in Chad to nearly 20% in Gabon; a parallel CEMAC/AFRISTAT industrial-production-index workshop (Douala, 10-14 August) worked toward a binding community statistical regulation

subject: data.statistics
name: ICT benchmarking across Central Africa
milestone: Funded at USD 1,368,579 for the regulators and statistics offices
position_end: Funded to benchmark ICTs across the zone's telecommunications regulators and national statistics offices (2021)
note: No published benchmarking output under it is held.

subject: data.satellite
name: CREWS Central Africa (hydrometeorological early-warning network)
milestone: Regional flood-forecasting training and data-management framework, March 2026
position_end: Sub-regional observing and forecasting network feeding the WMO's WIS/WHOS systems, with RSMC-Yaounde issuing regional severe-weather guidance and an ECCAS Situation Room operational at CAPC-AC Douala since September 2024, part of the continental AMHEWAS early-warning system; co-financed by the EU's SEWA programme (US$2m) and the World Bank (US$10m, across Chad, the Central African Republic, Rwanda and the DRC). Three further steps are on the record: a November 2025 remote training that had national and regional hydrologists apply satellite precipitation, soil-moisture and water-level altimetry alongside in-situ measurement across the Niger, Chad and Congo basins; a February 2026 agreement on communication and collaboration mechanisms for producing and disseminating early warnings; and a March 2026 regional flood-forecasting training with a data-management framework spanning the community and river-basin memberships
note: Captured under a proxy date as a standing project page rather than a single dated news event
